first.rationale: The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point directly at the funnel stage that memory_86 and memory_31 both say responds to simplification, so simplify_onboarding is the best-matched lever for the single slot. I am spending the verification budget on exactly those two memories because they are the load-bearing evidence for my choice and because they may not be independent: 'shortening onboarding' (day 52) and 'cutting required fields at signup' (day 12) could be one underlying experiment consolidated twice, which would make my support look twice as strong as it is. I want the original records to check whether the lifts were measured on distinct cohorts and whether either tracked downstream qualified revenue rather than just activation counts. I am not spending budget on memory_73: the competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the tempting response, but the memory already carries its own explicit caveat that it materially reduced 30-day retention and should not be generalized, and the primary objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so competitive pressure is exactly the condition under which that caveat matters most, not a reason to discount it. Downstream risk to flag: cutting signup fields can degrade lead routing and qualification data, and memory_44 says enterprise prospects convert through sales-assisted demo paths, so a simplification that collapses the demo-request path would trade durable pipeline quality for self-serve activation counts. The experiment should keep the enterprise path intact and instrument qualified-revenue and 30-day retention, not just completion rate. Running at standard scale rather than broad rollout because the prior lifts were measured on SMB self-serve in a different quarter and may not transfer to current conditions; if verification shows the two memories are a single duplicated result, I would drop to a small guarded test rather than switch levers.

final.rationale: Verification resolved my main worry: exp_86 and exp_31 are distinct experiments with different metric sets and different intervention points (flow length vs. signup fields), not one result consolidated twice. So the support for simplify_onboarding is genuinely two independent confirmations, and it remains the lever best matched to the two metrics that are actually declining (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%). Notably exp_86 showed 30-day retention +3%, which is the opposite sign from promotional pricing's retention damage — that is the distinguishing evidence for the sustainable-revenue objective. I am not switching to promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 carries an explicit do-not-generalize caveat grounded in a material 30-day retention drop, and competitive pressure is the condition that makes that caveat binding, not one that suspends it. Remaining uncertainty I am deliberately not papering over: exp_86 never reported qualified revenue at all, only completion, time-to-value and retention, so the link from onboarding improvement to the primary objective is inferred rather than measured. exp_31 did measure qualified revenue at +4%, but the record states it holds on SMB and was not replicated on other segments, and it showed a small retention dip of -1%. Both priors are also from a pre-competitor market; the current quarter may not reproduce them. That is why I am running a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout. Downstream value risk stands: memory_44 says enterprise converts through the sales-assisted demo path, and neither verified record covers enterprise, so the simplification must be scoped to the self-serve SMB funnel and must not collapse or de-prioritize the demo-request route. Instrument qualified revenue and 30-day retention as primary readouts, not completion rate alone, since completion is the metric most likely to improve for reasons that do not convert into durable revenue.
